newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrican rightist gets jail term for beating blacks.
newsitem.headline: SAfrican rightist gets jail term for beating blacks.

text.p: South African white supremacist leader Eugene Terre Blanche was sentenced to six years in jail on Tuesday for trying to murder one black man and assaulting another.

"On count one, the accused is sentenced to six years imprisonment. On charge two, the accused is sentenced to a period of one year imprisonment, which will be served concurrently," said magistrate Chris Eksteen.

The court adjourned for a break and Eksteen was expected to rule later on whether Terre Blanche, leader of the neo-Nazi Afrikaner Resistance Movement (AWB), would be given the right to appeal against the sentences and convictions.
Several dozen right-wingers in khaki were at the court to show support for their leader, while scores of police guarded the courtroom and used razor-wire to seal off the road outside it.
Around a hundred blacks gathered nearby and some waved placards calling for a life jail term for Terre Blanche.

The supremacist leader rallied thousands of rightists behind his cause during negotiations to end apartheid in the early 1990s, but his support has waned in recent years largely because of South Africa's peaceful transition to majority rule, instead of the bloodbath he had forecast.
